item.title: China's logistics sees improved performance as industrial upgrades support growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
BEIJING, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- China's logistics demand maintained steady growth in the first three quarters of the year, supported by industrial upgrading and resilient high-end manufacturing, official data showed Sunday.
The total value of national social logistics reached 280 trillion yuan (about 41.7 trillion U.S. dollars) in the January-September period, up 4.9 percent year on year, according to data from the China Federation of Logistics and Purchasing.
In the first three quarters, the value of industrial goods logistics rose 5.3 percent year on year, contributing 78 percent to the growth of the total.
Within this growth, equipment manufacturing and high-tech manufacturing played a prominent leading role, with their shares rising to 37.6 percent and 18.3 percent, respectively, according to the federation.
Logistics volumes for new products such as smart wristbands, 3D printing equipment and sensors surged 77.1 percent, 62.5 percent and 16.4 percent year on year, respectively, highlighting an accelerated shift toward new and upgraded industrial logistics demand, the data showed.
From January to September, the total cost of social logistics reached 14.8 trillion yuan, up 4.2 percent year on year. The ratio of total social logistics costs to GDP stood at 13.8 percent, down 0.2 percentage points from the same period last year.
"The dividends of logistics cost reduction continue to be released to the real economy," said Liu Yuhang, chief engineer of the federation.
Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, Liu said that with the arrival of the e-commerce peak season and the year-end production rush, logistics demand is expected to be released in a concentrated manner.
High-quality logistics development will provide strong support for the recovery of the real economy and the achievement of the full-year economic and social development goals, he said.

item.title: Small producers, big markets -- the CIIE story
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
This photo taken on Oct. 26, 2026 shows the south square of the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai), the main venue for the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), in east China's Shanghai. (Xinhua/Fang Zhe)
by Maya Majueran
At a time when global trade is increasingly disturbed by tariffs, protectionism and geopolitical competition, a different story is emerging from Shanghai's exhibition halls.
It is not about multinational giants or the strategic interests of major economies. It is about Peruvian artisans, Kenyan avocado farmers and Malagasy herders -- ordinary producers seeking access to international markets and opportunities to improve their livelihoods.
The China International Import Expo (CIIE) is helping turn "inclusive globalization" from a diplomatic slogan into economic reality by creating market opportunities, generating employment, and improving livelihoods.
For many developing countries, the greatest obstacle to international trade is not a lack of products or entrepreneurial ambition, but limited access to markets, financing, logistics and commercial networks. Through targeted support, dedicated exhibition areas for least-developed countries, and direct connections with Chinese buyers, the CIIE seeks to reduce these barriers.
The objective is not charity, but meaningful participation in global trade.
The CIIE's significance also lies in its continuity. Through its "6 days + 365 days" model, the expo connects temporary exhibitions with year-round trading platforms. Bonded warehousing, cross-border e-commerce, and buyer matchmaking help businesses turn initial orders into sustained commercial relationships.
In July 2025, Burundi shipped 38.4 tonnes of Arabica coffee directly to China for the first time, followed by contracts exceeding 900 tonnes worth over 5 million U.S. dollars.
A visitor learns about coffee at the pavilion of Burundi during the eighth China International Import Expo (CIIE) in east China's Shanghai, Nov. 7, 2025. (Xinhua/Ren Pengfei)
At the seventh CIIE in 2024, 13 of 16 participating Nigerian companies reportedly secured agreements, including a cocoa contract worth over 1.2 million dollars.
The eighth CIIE last year recorded 83.49 billion dollars in one-year intended deals, up 4.4 percent from the previous edition and hitting a new high.
Smaller economies face structural disadvantages in international trade. Regulatory compliance, logistics, marketing, and distribution impose disproportionately high costs on low-volume exporters. By connecting buyers and sellers and facilitating market entry, the CIIE helps reduce these barriers.
The CIIE offers one practical model for smaller economies to access international markets. For artisans in Peru, farmers in Kenya, and herding communities in Madagascar, the benefits can extend beyond export contracts to employment, household incomes and local development.
Inclusive globalization should be measured not simply by how much trade expands, but by how widely its opportunities are shared.
It is an approach worth drawing on.

item.title: Xi stresses China, Oman partnership in energy, investment, high-tech innovation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang)
BEIJING, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Monday that China stands ready to deepen the alignment of development strategies with Oman, turning the two countries into stable and reliable partners in energy, partners with great potential in investment, and partners in high-tech innovation.
Xi made the remarks during talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China.
This marks the first visit to China by Oman's head of state since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries 48 years ago.

item.title: China's "porcelain capital" wins Global Award for Sustainable Development in Cities
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
This file photo shows a view of the Taoyangli Historical and Cultural Block in Jingdezhen, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Xinhua)
FUZHOU, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- The global observance of 2026 World Cities Day was held on Saturday in east China's Fuzhou, with five cities, including China's "porcelain capital" Jingdezhen, honored with the fourth-cycle Global Award for Sustainable Development in Cities, also known as the Shanghai Award.
The event runs from Oct. 31 to Nov. 2. Apart from Jingdezhen, the other four recipients of the Shanghai Award, which recognizes cities for achievements in sustainable urban development, are Addis Ababa in Ethiopia, Santiago de Cali in Colombia, Istanbul in Türkiye, and Katowice in Poland.
The event brings together senior United Nations officials alongside representatives from national governments, local authorities, international organizations, academic institutions, the private sector, and community networks to share best practices and advance practical solutions to common urban challenges.
In December 2013, the 68th United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution designating Oct. 31 as World Cities Day starting in 2014. It was the first international day proposed by the Chinese government at the United Nations.
Ceramic culture has long been an ideal medium for cross-civilization dialogue. As a cornerstone commodity of the ancient Silk Road, Jingdezhen porcelain was a defining cultural symbol, through which the world came to know China and China reached out to the world.
Building on this legacy, Jingdezhen has embraced a model of development that combines cultural preservation with creative renewal. Former porcelain factories have been reimagined as cultural and creative districts, old streets are lined with ceramic-themed installations, and historic neighborhoods have been carefully preserved and revitalized.
The city is home to more than 3,200 inheritors of intangible cultural heritage in ceramic craftsmanship. It has also been named in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network as a City of Crafts and Folk Art.
Jingdezhen's recognition is just one example of China's broader urban renewal efforts.
Urban renewal also holds huge potential for investment and consumption. China has set a target of renovating 1,500 old streets and factory compounds from 2026 to 2030, bringing in new industries and business models to inject fresh momentum into urban development.
"Converting old streets and factory sites into cultural and creative districts drives growth in dining, retail and entertainment," said Yan Yuejin, deputy director of the E-house China R&D Institute.
